speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what are the overall measures to assist the vulnerable in the community such as cardboard collectors, beggars, rough sleepers and pedlars; and (b) what are the ways by which the Ministry can better and continually communicate to the public on the help measures available so that longer term sustainable support can be given to these vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For clients who require employment support, we link them up with Workforce Singapore or the Employment and Employability Institute.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For clients with housing or other social issues, we similarly link them up with the relevant agencies accordingly to help resolve their issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In parallel, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) continues to work with community partners to reach out to and befriend those who may be more vulnerable in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: PEERS Network partners engage rough sleepers and may refer them to overnight community-based shelters, known as Safe Sound Sleeping Places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Rough sleepers who require short-term accommodation and onsite social work intervention to secure stable housing can seek shelter at MSF-funded Transitional Shelters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Social workers at the Transitional Shelters work with individuals to address their various underlying social issues and progress towards stable long-term housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, VIC partners refer individuals needing financial assistance to Social Service Offices (SSOs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If other forms of assistance are required, the SSOs link them up with the relevant help agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF regularly shares information on the various available schemes and initiatives, including outreach efforts, through various public communication platforms such as the media, MSF website, MSF Facebook and MSFCares, an electronic newsletter which is disseminated to our partners to keep them connected with news and updates from MSF Family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This includes documentary series and videos which showcase various social issues and the support for beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: One example would be news stories on the efforts by our charity food workgroup to tackle the issue of food insecurity and the coordination of food support for those in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Another example would be MSF's collaboration with Nanyang Polytechnic students to produce a video featuring PEERS Network partners, such as Yio Chu Kang Chapel and Homeless Hearts of Singapore, who provide rough sleepers safe places to stay and help them navigate challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We also work with our partners such as other Government agencies, social service agencies, grassroots organisations and leaders, and our volunteers to raise public awareness of available assistance schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have plans to expand our engagement efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continue to feature the work of our existing partners to inform as well as inspire those who are interested to join our outreach and befriending efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We would also like to encourage members of the public who come across a rough sleeper, cardboard collector or tissue paper seller who is in need to contact the ComCare hotline at 1800-222-0000 or refer them to the nearest SSO for assistance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also pledge that organisations and ground partners, like our CDCs, will continue to work to assist the vulnerable in the community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A few supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Number one – obviously, there are many good programmes that are supporting existing vulnerable in the community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But looking at the communications channels listed by MSF, many people who want to help or who need help still would not naturally go to that official MSF channel.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I wonder if the Ministry could invest even more aggressively and effectively in communications to reach those who need help and those who are willing or want to offer to help, whether in print or social media, or TV and channels and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second one is to invest more in public education.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are many persons in the community, in the public, who, whatever their intentions are, have the habit of, for example, just taking a photograph or a video, and then posting it on social media, most of the time, without permission.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This kind of effort actually does not render sustainable help to the persons in need.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I think to discourage such habits which are actually not that effective and sometimes, not very respectful of those who need help, I wonder if the Ministry could consider investing even more in aggressive public education in this, so that, more can be helped in a more dignified way.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My third supplementary question is on the ComCare helpline.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I tried to call the ComCare helpline myself.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I find that the response is in English and by a machine to re-direct perhaps due to the need to triage the needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wonder if there is another more effective way of looking into beyond the ComCare line, to ensure that it is more effective.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Perhaps looking at different ways of doing it, for instance, setting up call centres that are actually answered by real persons and not by a machine.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I had earlier spent some time talking about befriending and MSF is very grateful to our various partners such as Central CDC and other befrienders who have worked with us.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Because we know that many of the vulnerable may not have a fixed abode, they may be moving from point to point.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And like what the Member mentioned, they may not automatically just walk into an SSO to seek help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we rely on our network of partners in the community to reach out to them, so that they see a physical face, trust is built, relationships are built.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And in so doing, some of these vulnerables may be more open to sharing about their underlying problems.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Only then, can we really address the root issues that led them to the current situation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The second point that the Member raised about public education, indeed, is a very important point.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I know that there are members of the public who feel that they may be helping the vulnerable by taking a photo, putting up a video.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I would urge that members of the public to be cautious when doing so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Because when you put up a video or a photo, apart from the fact that you might be infringing on the privacy as well as confidentiality of the vulnerable person, sometimes you may be bringing unwanted attention to the vulnerable person which may or may not lead to better outcomes for the person.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It might also worsen family relationships which sometimes are the underlying reasons why the vulnerable person is doing what he or she is doing.
